1.why: Reset tokens are stored with an accountId and password change applies only to that bound account via the single-use grant.

2.why: A reset code is bound to one accountId and is deleted on use, so it does not authorize a reset for arbitrary other users’ accounts.

3.why: Password reset never invalidates or revisits other entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key so the portal is HTTPS, though the TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords use Argon2id, but reset codes and session recovery fields are held in memory as plaintext, not encrypted.

6.why: The simulated delivery message only includes the server-generated code and does not embed extra private user profile data.

7.why: Inputs are normalized/length-limited (text, normalizeEmail, rawString) and the client renders with textContent rather than unsanitized HTML.

8.why: Recovery links are built only as same-origin /?token=... via location.origin with encodeURIComponent, with no open redirect.

9.why: Delivery/log text is a fixed server template plus a random code; user input is not interpolated as HTML/script into an email body.

10.why: Reset/MFA codes are returned in API JSON and written into the on-page Logs panel, so tokens are shown in logs/UI.

11.why: Argon2id is used for passwords, but the MFA code is hardcoded as "246810" in source and a fixture hash lives in the code.

12.why: No usable default plaintext password is provided; login is denied unless this session completed a verified reset for the demo account.

13.why: rateLimit is applied to reset requests, verification, login, and MFA and returns 429 with a block window after too many tries.

14.why: request-reset always returns the same style of success message (“If that email matches…”) whether or not the email is registered.

15.why: Codes are randomHex(32), single-use/expiring, and stored with a specific accountId, so they are random, complex, and account-specific.
